title: A team's walks as training data: one example per hand-off, the board before and after, under consent
request: Phase 6 (the owner): capture, record and store everything the teams do for training the solver model.
plan: A builder in dclab_core for a walk's hand-offs.
The studio assembles the walks from the orchestra files under consent.
The lake maps each hand-off to a family; a walk with a model is a teacher's.

decisions.decision: One example per hand-off, the board before the node and after it.
decisions.why: The board is what the team knew; the change a node made to it is what the solver model must learn to make.

decisions.decision: A family per node: design and routes, the audit, the run, the report, the critic's send-back, the rest agent steps.
decisions.why: The lake's families are how Model 1's corpus is balanced and judged; a node's work belongs to one of them.

decisions.decision: A walk in which a model was asked is evaluation only.
decisions.why: The owner's rule: Claude's outputs are evaluation material; DCLab's own rules' walks are gold.

change: dclab_core.datasets.team_walks and TEAM_FAMILY (dclab-core 0.70.0, DatasetManifest v7, v6 read as v7); dclab_rnd/datasets.py _team_items and the set team_walks/boards; the lake's mapping of the set.

findings.defect: A walk that used Claude could be labelled DCLab's own and land in train.
findings.scenario: The datasets build ran while a walk waited at the build approval: its Claude critic's send-back became ask_question, rule_prod, train; a restarted thread took another walk's record.
findings.cause: Walks were paired with records by position, and no record read as no spend.
findings.fix: Every board line carries its walk's id; walks.jsonl keeps each walk's record by that id; a walk with no record is left out, never guessed.

findings.defect: Two walks merged when the second began with an answered pause.
findings.scenario: The version a closed pause raised made the second walk's first hand-off look like the first walk's next.
findings.cause: A new walk was detected by the board's version.

findings.defect: Spend > 0 missed models that cost nothing.
findings.scenario: A critic on a local or an unpriced model made its answers rule_prod gold: a student trained on its own output.
findings.cause: The origin was read from the spend.
findings.fix: The walk keeps the models its requests were answered by; Claude's a teacher's (evaluation only), another model's left out, none DCLab's own.

findings.defect: A deleted project's draft walk left under the workspace switch alone.
findings.scenario: Draft d1 built p1, whose train switch is off; p1 deleted; d1's walk was exported.
findings.cause: The draft's project being gone made it a draft without a project.
findings.fix: A draft whose project was deleted never leaves.

findings.defect: The person's words left unredacted in labels, part titles and blockers.
findings.scenario: labels 'Maria Lopez keeps them, call +44 20 ...' stayed raw.
findings.cause: Only some problem fields were redacted.
findings.fix: labels, part titles, workflow names and blockers redacted as every exported text.

findings.defect: A walk written while the workspace was at operate left once training was switched on.
findings.scenario: The hand-off events were refused by their level; the board lines were not.
findings.fix: Each board line and walk record carries the consent level it was written under; only lines that may leave for training leave.

findings.defect: A deletion that removed only orchestra lines did not mark the sets stale.
findings.scenario: Events already purged by retention; the deleted walk's rows stayed in the built set.
findings.cause: The stale marker looked at events and decisions only.
findings.fix: The orchestra lines removed count too.

findings.defect: The person's decisions were taught as the rules'.
findings.scenario: kept_by_person on a leak suspect became leakage_judgment, rule_prod.
findings.cause: No origin for a hand-off that closed a pause.
findings.fix: A hand-off that closed a pause is human_exposed.

findings.defect: Some nodes had the wrong family.
findings.scenario: plan_workflow fell to agent_step; route never reached the board.
findings.cause: The mapping missed the understanding walk's workflow node.
findings.fix: plan_workflow is solution_design; the routes are in the design's board.

findings.defect: The no-value check could never fail and many paths were untested.
findings.scenario: The test looked for another fixture's marker.
findings.cause: A convenient check, not the project's own values.
findings.fix: The project's own order ids checked; a test per finding.

outcome: Every walk of both teams reaches the training lake under consent, a hand-off at a time.
lessons: Keep the shared state of a multi-agent run whole at every hand-off: the training example is the difference between two boards.
Pair two records by an id written into both, never by their order: an unfinished run shifts every pairing after it.
risks: Walks are few until testers and projects run through the teams.
